answer: Login times cluster: one operator logs in around the same hours each day, with a spread that reflects real life. The network fits the login-time distribution per account and flags a session that lands far outside the cluster, especially when many accounts log in at the same minute. Like a orchard in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. A tide alone is noise; a sonnet of consistent sessions is a pattern the network can trust.
